stop_trigger_rule.rule: A stop is triggered by a DAILY CLOSE below the level, not by an intraday print. Same for targets.
why: ETH is the only position whose trigger condition was ever written down, and it says 'if price CLOSES below the stop, convert ALL to USDT'. This makes the book consistent rather than inventing a new convention.
The stop LEVEL is computed from daily closes (close - 3 x ATR14). A level derived from closes but triggered intraday is internally inconsistent.

Decisive: this system observes prices ONCE a day at 07:10 UTC and notifies once a day. An intraday stop is not executable here - claiming an exit at 11.337 would mean claiming a fill at a price nobody observed and nobody could have acted on. That is the August bookkeeping failure repeating.
stop_trigger_rule.honesty_note: This is being written down AFTER the ambiguous event, and it resolves in the direction that keeps the LINK position alive. That is uncomfortable and is recorded rather than glossed. The three reasons above are outcome-independent, and the rule now binds in both directions: a close below a stop exits even if the position recovers intraday afterwards.
stop_trigger_rule.cost_disclosed: A close-based stop does NOT fill at the stop level. With one observation a day, the exit happens at the next daily reading, which can be well below the stop. Yesterday I wrote 'if it fires it fires near +17.1%' - that was imprecise, and the realistic fill is worse than the level.

engine_fix_2026_10_14.found: Both of today's band changes were artefacts of the same mechanism, in opposite directions.
engine_fix_2026_10_14.mechanism: resolve_states() debounces trend_state with a 0.5% buffer around the 50-day average, so a hairline cross raises no trend alert. The SCORING has no buffer: the price-vs-50-day term is the largest single component at +/-25 and flips the instant price crosses. A cross of a tenth of a percent therefore moves the score 50 points and fires a band-change alert that the trend logic deliberately suppressed.

todays_two_cases.BNBUSDT: BUY 35 -> HOLD -15 while sitting 0.14% BELOW its 50-day (743.35 against 744.38).
todays_two_cases.ADCB: SELL -25 -> BUY 25 while sitting 0.42% ABOVE its own (15.92 against 15.85). Opposite direction, same mechanism, on a +1.02% day.

engine_fix_2026_10_14.adcb_was_caught_by_a_different_guard: ADCB produced NO alert at all, because the anti-whipsaw rule saw BUY (Oct 12) -> SELL (Oct 13) -> BUY (Oct 14) and suppressed the repeat. That guard, added for exactly this, earned its keep today and independently confirms the move is churn.
engine_fix_2026_10_14.fix_made: Added _hairline_note(), which labels a band-change alert when the 50-day term flipped and price is inside the 0.5% buffer. This changes alert WORDING only. It is the same pattern as _stretch_note, which labels a band change caused only by the RSI/Bollinger term.
engine_fix_2026_10_14.fix_not_made_deliberately: I did NOT add a deadband to the scoring's trend term. It would reprice the entire board and break comparability with 90 days of recorded scores, and that is not a change to make unilaterally mid-cycle. Proposed below with a measurement instead.

deadband_asymmetry_proposal.observation: The scoring protects its SMALLER term and not its larger one. The 20/50 structure term (+/-15) is gated by MA_DEADBAND so it is not scored when the averages are within 0.5% of each other. The price-vs-50-day trend term (+/-25) has no gate at all.

measurement.method: For the 20 instruments that supply bar history, over the last 180 completed days each (3,360 observations), counted how often the close sits within +/-0.5% of its own 50-day average, and what share of 50-day SIDE CHANGES land inside that buffer.
measurement.hairline_share: 35% - roughly one in three 50-day crosses is a hairline the trend debounce suppresses while the score acts on it at full +/-25.
measurement.worst_offenders: DIB 57%, XRP 56%, BNB 55%, TECOM 52%. The measurement independently fingers the names I had already muted for band churn by eye - TECOM, DEWA and TALABAT - which is the strongest evidence that this is the mechanism behind that churn rather than a separate problem.
measurement.cleanest: ETH: 1 of 180 observations in the buffer (0.6%) and 0 of 3 crosses hairline. Its cross on 2026-10-13 was decisive, which is worth knowing given it triggered the exit.

deadband_asymmetry_proposal.proposal: Gate the trend term the same way the structure term is gated: when |close/sma50 - 1| < MA_DEADBAND, do not score it and say 'price within 0.5% of the 50-day - no trend edge (not scored)'. That would make a hairline cross worth 0 rather than a 50-point swing, and would align the score with the trend_state buffer that already exists.
deadband_asymmetry_proposal.cost_of_the_change: It would reprice every historical score, so comparisons against the 90-day record would break unless the record is annotated. It would also mute some genuine early crosses - ETH's 2026-10-13 cross was 1.08% clear so it would still have scored, but a slower roll-over might score 0 for a few sessions before confirming.
deadband_asymmetry_proposal.status: NOT IMPLEMENTED. Recorded with its measurement so the decision rests on 219 observed crosses rather than on today's two anecdotes. This is a design change to make deliberately, at a review, not inside a daily cycle.

uae_data_lag_2026_10_14.issue: The Yahoo UAE series publishes the most recent completed session LATE, by about a day.
uae_data_lag_2026_10_14.evidence: Yesterday's 07:09 UTC snapshot held bars ending 10-08 then 10-13 (the in-progress bar) - Monday 10-12 was ABSENT. Today's snapshot holds 10-08, 10-12 and 10-14, and Tuesday 10-13 is now the one absent. Monday's bar materialised a day after Monday.
uae_data_lag_2026_10_14.consequence_for_averages: UAE sma20/sma50 are therefore computed over a series missing the latest one or two sessions. Combined with the four-day week, the last 50 UAE bars span 86 calendar days against roughly 70 for a clean five-day 50-session window - the window reaches about 23% further back in time than the crypto equivalent. In a falling market that biases the average toward older, higher prices and makes price look MORE below its average than it is. That plausibly contributed to how extreme yesterday's UAE reading was.
uae_data_lag_2026_10_14.consequence_for_stops: This bites the fix I made yesterday. last_completed_close() returns the newest bar dated before today, which for a UAE name can be a TWO-session-old close. If a UAE position is ever opened, its stop would be tested against a stale close. Added to the limitation already recorded for the ADX/TradingView names, which have no bars at all and fall back to the live tick.
uae_data_lag_2026_10_14.not_fixed: No code change. The honest options are to carry the lag or to stop rating UAE names until their bar settles, and the second is worse - it would blind the board for a day at a time. Recorded so the averages are read with it in mind.

uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.resolved: 2026-10-19. Five days after first noticing it, the Friday anomaly is explained.
uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.the_mechanism: FRIDAY IS A TRADING SESSION. The data source serves Friday's bar TRANSIENTLY - it is visible on the Saturday and Sunday runs - and then DELETES it when Monday's bar appears. That is why a year of history holds zero Fridays.
evidence: On Sat 2026-10-17 and Sun 2026-10-18 a settled Friday bar existed for ALL TEN Yahoo UAE names with genuine OHLC and real intraday ranges (EMIRATESNBD O 31.28 H 31.62 L 30.92 C 31.58).
Today it is GONE from all ten, and the weekday distribution is back to exactly zero Fridays (EMAAR: Mon 51, Tue 52, Wed 52, Thu 51, Fri 0).
Monday's OPEN equals the Friday close we observed, exactly, on three of five checked names - EMIRATESNBD 31.58, SALIK 5.21, TECOM 3.23. Friday really did trade and close there.

uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.MATERIAL_CONSEQUENCE: Every UAE moving average is permanently computed over a series missing ONE SESSION IN FIVE. This is not a lag that catches up - the Friday bars are deleted, so the hole is permanent. It explains the measurement I took on 2026-10-14 and misread: the last 50 UAE bars span 86 calendar days against roughly 70 for a clean five-day window. So a UAE '50-day average' actually reaches back about 12.5 calendar weeks instead of 10, biasing it toward older prices and systematically mis-stating how far price sits from it.
uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.bearing_on_todays_signals: This degrades every UAE trend call, including EMIRATESNBD's STRONG BUY, which rests on being 2.2% above a 50-day computed from 80% of the actual sessions. It does not make the signal worthless - direction is probably robust to a uniform 20% sampling of sessions - but the precise distances are not trustworthy and should not be quoted as though they were.
uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.proposed_fix: The weekend run SEES the Friday bar before it is deleted, so Friday bars can be captured on Saturday or Sunday, persisted locally, and merged back into the series. That fixes Fridays going FORWARD but not the year of history, so the 50-day average stays contaminated for roughly ten weeks until enough captured Fridays accumulate.
uae_friday_mystery_SOLVED_2026_10_19.not_built_today: Deliberately not implemented. No UAE position can be opened while Al Ramz is shut, so a persistence layer today is premature engineering. But this should be fixed BEFORE the first UAE trade rather than after, and it is now the top item on that list - every UAE trend signal is currently computed on four fifths of the sessions.

CORRECTION_2026_10_20.what_i_claimed: That the anomaly was SOLVED: Friday bars are served on the weekend and deleted when Monday's appears.
CORRECTION_2026_10_20.what_today_shows: Monday 2026-10-19's bar is ALSO missing today - the series reads Oct 13, 14, 15, then today's Oct 20. So deletion is not Friday-specific, or there is a rolling lag on top of it.
CORRECTION_2026_10_20.best_current_model: Two effects. (1) The most recent completed session is often absent for a day or two before being backfilled - the 'publication lag' I described on Oct 14 and then wrongly dismissed on Oct 16. (2) Friday sessions are never backfilled at all, which is why a year of history holds 50+ of every other weekday and zero Fridays.
CORRECTION_2026_10_20.prediction_set_in_advance: If this model is right, Monday Oct 19 reappears within a day or two and Friday Oct 16 never does. Checked on the next runs.
CORRECTION_2026_10_20.pattern_worth_naming: This is the THIRD time in a week I have announced a confident explanation of this source's dates (Oct 14 four-day week, Oct 16 forward date-stamp, Oct 19 'SOLVED'), and each was partly overturned within a day or two. The operational conclusions have survived every revision: Fridays are missing from the averages, the newest sessions may be missing when read, and no decision should depend on a UAE bar's date. I will state predictions rather than solutions from here.
